info.title: Atlas API
info.description:
The Atlas API connects your merchant systems to G2 Atlas. Merchants you add are screened by G2 before you approve them and monitored by G2 after, and your systems receive the results and record your decisions, without file uploads or work in the Atlas screens.

**What you can do**

- **Screen new merchants.** Add a merchant to Onboarding, one at a time or up to 100 in one request, and approve or reject it once G2 has reviewed its websites.
- **Monitor approved merchants.** Add merchants to Monitoring the same way. G2 rescans them on your portfolio's cadence for each service (CC, MCC, GRAPH). Add a merchant to the monitoring cycle or remove it at any time.
- **Track your merchants.** Get a merchant by its id, or list merchants by bulk request, portfolio, status or date range, so your records match Atlas.
- **Act on what G2 finds.** List a merchant's findings and mark them as risk or no risk. Approve, reject or terminate the merchant. A terminated merchant cannot be reinstated.
- **Keep merchant details current.** Update one merchant or up to 100 at once; only the fields you send change.
- **Share the outcome.** Download a merchant's Merchant Summary report, a PDF of its identity, risk and findings with evidence, once it has been requested in Atlas.

**How it works**

A merchant belongs to one portfolio. In a bulk request, each merchant is saved or rejected on its own: the response lists the result for every merchant and a bulkId to retrieve them later. Every endpoint needs an OAuth 2.0 client-credentials token.

**Request id.** Every response carries an `X-Request-Id` header. Quote it when contacting support.

**Timeouts.** Set the client timeout to at least 60 seconds; bulk requests and merchants with many stores take longer.

**Rate limits.** Requests over the limit get 429. Retry with exponential backoff.

**Retries.** 502 and 503 are safe to retry for reads. Retrying a merchant create that succeeded returns 409 MERCHANT_ALREADY_EXISTS.

get.description: Returns a page of merchants. Omit the filters to list all merchants in your account. clientMerchantKey matches exactly and case-sensitively; URL-encode the value. portfolioId restricts results to merchants in that portfolio. When both filters are sent, both must match. items is empty when no merchants match. Omit cursor for the first page; pass nextCursor unchanged with the same filters and size to fetch the next page. When nextCursor is absent, there are no more results.

patch.summary: Set a merchant's review status and add it to or remove it from Monitoring
patch.description: Records your decision on a merchant and sets whether G2 monitors it. After G2 screens a merchant you added to Onboarding, send your decision in merchantStatus and, to move the merchant to Monitoring, monitoringStatus ACTIVE in the same request; PAUSED removes it from monitoring. A field you leave out is unchanged, and neither field affects the other.

status.description: PENDING: queued. GENERATING: being built. READY: reportDownloadUrl is set. FAILED: request a new one.

lastName.description: The person's last name, for PRINCIPAL contacts. Kept on the contact for your records. G2 monitors the person by the name field, so put the full name there too

name.description: Full name of the person (PRINCIPAL) or the company name (BUSINESS); part of the identity G2 monitors the merchant against. firstName and lastName are not, so set name even when you send them

stores.description: The merchant's stores, one per URL. If any of them cannot be added, the merchant is not created and the request fails with 422.

mccs.description: The MCCs you have on file. If MCC checking is on for the portfolio, a finding is raised when the store's business does not match them.

billingDescriptor.description: The name shown on cardholder statements

contacts.description: The merchant's people or business contacts as you have them on file. Their names, emails, phones and addresses are part of the identity G2 monitors the merchant against.

MerchantConflictError.description: The error returned when a merchant cannot be created because one already exists, carrying a machine-readable code alongside the standard error fields.

instance.description: Request path that caused the problem

clientMerchantKey.description: The clientMerchantKey that is already taken

existingMerchantId.description: Id of the merchant holding that key; may be absent

UpdatePortfolioMerchantRequest.description: The merchant's review and monitoring status in a portfolio to change; send at least one field

merchantStatus.description: Your review decision for the merchant in this portfolio: TO_REVIEW (not reviewed yet), IN_PROCESS (being reviewed), APPROVED, REJECTED or TERMINATED. Approve or reject a merchant after Onboarding or after Monitoring. REJECTED does not change monitoringStatus. TERMINATED also cancels the merchant's snoozes in this portfolio; finding statuses and monitoringStatus are left as they are. Once TERMINATED, merchantStatus cannot be changed: sending it returns 409, as does sending the status the merchant already has.

monitoringStatus.description: Whether G2 keeps scanning the merchant in this portfolio: ACTIVE or PAUSED. PAUSED stops monitoring scans until it is set back to ACTIVE; merchantStatus, findings and snoozes are left as they are. Sending the status the merchant already has changes nothing.

UpdateMerchantRequest.description: Fields to change on a merchant. All are optional; a null or absent field is left unchanged.

legalName.description: The merchant's registered company name. It is part of the identity G2 monitors the merchant against. Cannot be cleared.

contacts.description: The merchant's people or business contacts as you have them on file. Their names, emails, phones and addresses are part of the identity G2 monitors the merchant against. Replaces the list; [] clears it.

mids.description: Your acquirer merchant IDs (MIDs) for this merchant. They are part of the identity G2 monitors the merchant against. Replaces the list; [] clears it.

dbas.description: The merchant's trading names (DBAs). Replaces the list; [] clears it.

mccs.description: Replaces the MCC list; [] clears it.

productsServicesDescription.description: What the merchant sells. "" clears it.

mastercardIca.description: Your acquirer's Mastercard ICA (4-6 digits). "" clears it.

visaBin.description: Your acquirer's Visa BIN (6 or 8 digits). "" clears it.

billingDescriptor.description: The name shown on cardholder statements. "" clears it.

updatedAt.description: When the portfolio was last updated

PortfolioProduct.description: A product on a portfolio; it scans only when at least one of its checks (ccEnabled, mccEnabled, graphEnabled) is on

productType.description: Which product this is: ONBOARDING, the one-time scan of each new merchant, or MONITORING, the scheduled rescans of the portfolio's merchants

ccEnabled.description: Whether content compliance checking is on: when it is, scans review the store's content and raise a finding for each risk category found

mccEnabled.description: Whether MCC checking is on: when it is, scans compare the store's business with the merchant's reported MCC and raise a finding on a mismatch

graphEnabled.description: Whether connected-store discovery is on: when it is, scans also find stores connected to the merchant's stores, which appear with connected=true and their own findings

cadences.description: Scan cadence of each service enabled on this product: one entry per service among CC, MCC and GRAPH

MerchantPage.description: One cursor page of merchants matching the supplied filters

nextCursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page; absent when there are no more results

Finding.description: A finding detected on one of the merchant's stores

findingId.description: ID of the finding. Use it for status and comment calls.

storeId.description: Store the finding was detected on. Pass it as storeId when snoozing.

url.description: The address that was scanned when the finding was raised: the store's URL or another page of the same store, such as the page it redirects to. Use it as the link a reviewer opens to check the finding.

redirectedUrl.description: Redirect (61) findings only: the address the store redirects to. Absent on other findings, and on Redirect findings whose evidence does not name an address.

categoryId.description: What kind of issue this is. Findings of the same category on the same store are reviewed as one item in Atlas UI. mccDetection tells MCC detections apart from other findings.

categoryName.description: Readable name of the category, for display

status.description: Your review decision on this finding. It stays TO_REVIEW until someone sets it. It returns to TO_REVIEW when a FINDING snooze that selected it ends or is cancelled. A URL snooze on its store also resets it when it ends or is cancelled.

riskSeverity.description: How severe this finding is: the category's severity for your account, or NO_RISK once the finding is dismissed. Use it to prioritise review.

evidenceUrl.description: The page the evidence was seen on, as the scanner reported it. Usually a full URL on the scanned store, but it can be a bare host or N/A, so show it as text and use url as the link.

evidenceText.description: What the scanner found, as text to show a reviewer. Its form depends on the category: a JSON object (for example the detected email or phone in raw_entity, or keyword counts), an address for Online (59) and Redirect (61), or a short label such as UNSUPPORTED DOMAIN. Show it as text; its JSON keys are not part of the contract.

lastModifyDate.description: When a scan last wrote this finding (UTC). Setting a status does not change it.

snooze.description: The active snooze covering this finding; absent when not snoozed. A snoozed finding still counts toward the merchant's risk.

ignored.description: True when the store does not count toward the merchant's risk. Only stores G2 found connected to the merchant can be ignored: your portfolio is set to leave connected stores out of the risk, or a reviewer excluded the store in Atlas UI. Read-only; you can usually skip these findings.

mccDetection.description: True when the finding is an MCC detection: its category is a merchant category code the scan matched to the store's business, not an issue found on the store. False for every other finding.

snoozeId.description: ID of the snooze; use it to change or cancel the snooze

level.description: FINDING: this category on this store is snoozed. URL: the whole store is snoozed.

wakeDate.description: When the snooze ends; the findings then go back to TO_REVIEW.

Problem.description: The error body the API returns, as RFC 9457 problem details in application/problem+json. Branch on status and code, not on title or detail.

title.description: The HTTP reason phrase; do not branch on it

status.description: Same as the HTTP status; branch on this

detail.description: Human-readable reason for logs and support; the wording can change

instance.description: Request path that caused the problem

code.description: Machine-readable reason; branch on it, not on detail. One of INVALID_REQUEST (400), UNAUTHENTICATED (401), FORBIDDEN (403), NOT_FOUND (404), CONFLICT (409), RATE_LIMITED (429), INTERNAL_ERROR (500), BAD_GATEWAY (502), SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE (503), or MERCHANT_ALREADY_EXISTS (409 when creating a merchant whose clientMerchantKey is taken). New values may be added; when code is absent or unknown, branch on status

BulkCreateMerchantsRequest.description: Up to 100 merchants to create in one request

merchants.description: The merchants to create, 1 to 100. Each follows the rules of the single add.

BulkItemResult.description: Result for one item in a bulk request, in the order the items were sent

index.description: Position of the item in the request, starting at 0

clientMerchantKey.description: Your clientMerchantKey for the merchant in this item, as sent

merchantId.description: ID of the merchant created or updated. Absent when status is ERROR.

status.description: OK: saved. WARNING: saved, with a note in message. ERROR: not saved; message gives the reason.

field.description: Field that caused the WARNING or ERROR

message.description: Why the item has a WARNING or ERROR. Absent when status is OK.

BulkResponse.description: Outcome of a bulk request. Each item is saved or rejected on its own: valid items are saved and invalid items are reported, as in the Atlas file upload.

bulkId.description: Use to retrieve the merchants of this request with GET /api/v1/merchants?bulkId=

status.description: COMPLETED: every item OK. COMPLETED_WITH_ISSUES: at least one item has WARNING or ERROR. FAILED: no item was saved.

total.description: Number of items in the request

succeeded.description: Number of items saved, with status OK or WARNING

failed.description: Number of items not saved, with status ERROR

results.description: One result per item, in the order the items were sent

merchantId.description: ID of the merchant to update

BulkUpdateMerchantItem.description: Fields to change on one merchant; a field left out is unchanged

merchants.description: The merchants to update, 1 to 100. Each item names one merchant and the fields to change.

Cadence.description: When one service of a portfolio product runs its scheduled scans

service.description: The scan type this cadence applies to: CC, MCC or GRAPH, matching ccEnabled, mccEnabled and graphEnabled on the portfolio product

frequency.description: CUSTOM: a schedule that is not daily, weekly or monthly

hour.description: Hour of the day the scan starts, 0 to 23, in UTC

minute.description: Minute of the hour the scan starts, 0 to 59

findingIds.description: Findings of this merchant to update

status.description: The review decision to record; it replaces the finding's current status.

X-Request-Id.description: Identifier of this request. Quote it when contacting support.

oauth2.description: OAuth 2.0 client-credentials flow. Request an access token from the token URL with your client id, client secret and audience https://mlrc-external-api.everc.com/ (also published as x-audience), then send it as Authorization: Bearer. G2 links the client to your account when it sets the client up; a token without that link gets 403.
